claim_checks.claim: Edge-triggered (ET), with EPOLLET
claim_checks.page_says: EPOLLET Requests edge-triggered notification for the associated file descriptor.

claim_checks.claim: Several widely used event loops register with ET: the Go runtime
claim_checks.page_says: ev.Events = linux.EPOLLIN | linux.EPOLLOUT | linux.EPOLLRDHUP | linux.EPOLLET
claim_checks.note: The source shows that Go registers with EPOLLET. It cannot support 'widely used', which is the doc's own description added to the cited fact.

claim_checks.page_says: This is the callback that is used to add our wait queue to the target file wakeup lists. ... init_waitqueue_func_entry(&pwq->wait, ep_poll_callback);

claim_checks.section: ## 3. The actors and their data structures
claim_checks.claim: epoll instance (struct eventpoll): stores registrations in a red-black tree of epitems and queues ready ones on the ready list
claim_checks.page_says: /* List of ready file descriptors */ struct list_head rdllist; ... /* RB tree root used to store monitored fd structs */ struct rb_root_cached rbr;

claim_checks.section: ## 3. The actors and their data structures
claim_checks.claim: Each registration costs roughly 160 bytes on a 64-bit kernel, and /proc/sys/fs/epoll/max_user_watches caps the total per user
claim_checks.page_says: The limit is per real user ID. Each registered file descriptor costs roughly 90 bytes on a 32-bit kernel, and roughly 160 bytes on a 64-bit kernel.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLIN/EPOLLOUT unset: that direction is ignored: wakeups whose bits do not overlap the mask are dropped by the callback
claim_checks.page_says: not every device reports the events in the "key" parameter of the callback ... if (pollflags && !(pollflags & epi->event.events)) goto out_unlock;
claim_checks.note: The condition is missing. The callback drops a wakeup only when its key carries bits and none of them overlap. A wakeup with no bits passes, and the harvest re-poll filters it (`return res & epi->event.events`). Step 4 of the doc states this condition; §4 leaves it out.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLRDHUP since 2.6.17
claim_checks.page_says: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17)

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE unset: all instances are woken
claim_checks.page_says: The default in this scenario (when EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is not set) is for all epoll file descriptors to receive an event.

claim_checks.claim: All instances are woken (the [^exp] mark of that cell)
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: This mark cites only the local artifact. The [^ctl] mark on the same cell is S10.

claim_checks.claim: data field: opaque value returned with each event, from the latest ADD or MOD
claim_checks.page_says: The data field of each returned epoll_event structure contains the same data as was specified in the most recent call to epoll_ctl(2) (EPOLL_CTL_ADD, EPOLL_CTL_MOD)

claim_checks.claim: If a harvest is running, puts the epitem on the overflow list; otherwise links it on the ready list only if it is not already linked
claim_checks.page_says: if (ep_is_scanning(ep)) { if (!epi_on_ovflist(epi)) { ... } else if (!ep_is_linked(epi)) { /* In the usual case, add event to ready list. */

claim_checks.claim: That is why several writes before one epoll_wait produce one event (the [^exp] mark)
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: This mark cites only the local artifact. The [^epoll7] mark on the same sentence was not sampled.

claim_checks.claim: epoll_wait: if the ready list is empty, the thread adds itself to the instance's wait queue as an exclusive waiter and sleeps
claim_checks.page_says: eavail = ep_events_available(ep); if (!eavail) __add_wait_queue_exclusive(&ep->wq, &wait); ... return !list_empty_careful(&ep->rdllist) || ep_is_scanning(ep) ||
claim_checks.note: The condition is too wide. The thread sleeps only when no events are available, which also requires that no harvest (scan) is running. It does not sleep merely because the ready list is empty.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLONESHOT: reduces the mask to its private bits, so later callbacks see no requested event and ignore the item until EPOLL_CTL_MOD
claim_checks.page_says: if (epi->event.events & EPOLLONESHOT) { epi->event.events &= EP_PRIVATE_BITS; ... If the event mask does not contain any poll(2) event, we consider the descriptor to be disabled.

claim_checks.claim: Everything else that makes ET 'feel' different follows from that branch, plus one side channel: the mask, including the EPOLLET bit, travels to the driver as the poll key (step 2), and the pipe driver reads it (§6.3)
claim_checks.page_says: if ((filp->f_mode & FMODE_READ) && wait && (wait->_key & EPOLLET) &&
claim_checks.note: pipe.c shows the pipe driver reading EPOLLET from the poll key. It cannot support the claim that everything else about ET follows from the one branch and this one side channel. The poll-key path (`pt->_key = epi->event.events`) is on the [^src] page, which this sentence does not cite.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: 2048 bytes arrive; the app reads 1024 and waits again: no event, 1024 bytes stranded (the man page's pipe example)
claim_checks.page_says: edge-triggered mode delivers events only when changes occur on the monitored file descriptor ... the call to epoll_wait(2) done in step 5 might block indefinitely.
claim_checks.note: The man page's 2 kB / 1 kB example states the rule without a hedge. Its 'probably' and 'might' are about how long the wait lasts, not about whether an event arrives.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: New data while old data is still unread: new event on a pipe, AF_UNIX stream socket and TCP loopback (Linux 7.2.12), T4
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: Local artifact only.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: EPOLLET | EPOLLONESHOT, second write before re-arm: no event until EPOLL_CTL_MOD; the mask is disabled after delivery
claim_checks.page_says: the file descriptor is disabled in the interest list and no other events will be reported by the epoll interface. The user must call epoll_ctl() with EPOLL_CTL_MOD to rearm

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: Pipe filled to EAGAIN (65536 bytes), reader takes 1 byte: no EPOLLOUT, T8
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: 2019-12-07, Linus Torvalds, commit 1b6b26ae7053 'pipe: fix and clarify pipe write wakeup logic': a pipe write now wakes readers only if the pipe was empty before
claim_checks.page_says: [^kerrisk] 'Date: Sat Dec 7 12:14:28 2019 -0800 pipe: fix and clarify pipe write wakeup logic'; [^linus2020] 'we only wake up a reader of a pipe when we add data to it AND IT WAS EMPTY BEFORE.'
claim_checks.note: Grounded, but both sources are Rank 6 inside a role-3 section (see the KB-15 violations).

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: It ships in Linux 5.5
claim_checks.page_says: Between Linux 5.4 and 5.5 a regression was introduced in the operation of the epoll EPOLLET flag.
claim_checks.note: Kerrisk places the commit between 5.4 and 5.5. Grounded, but a Rank 6 source in role 3.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: realm-core expected an ET event on every write, using a pipe it does not drain until it fills
claim_checks.page_says: expected "edge triggered" be to "any new write will trigger it". ... it never drains the pipe until it is full.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: io_uring multishot polls set EPOLLET and get the same behaviour
claim_checks.page_says: Currently io_uring sets EPOLLET for multishot polls, so it gets the same behaviour.

claim_checks.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
claim_checks.claim: Drain until EAGAIN, and a missing 'per-write' event cannot hurt you
claim_checks.page_says: by waiting for an event only after read(2) or write(2) return EAGAIN. ... an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data.
claim_checks.note: epoll(7) suggests draining to EAGAIN. It never says that a missing per-write event is harmless; its text instead says an event is generated for each chunk of data. 'Cannot hurt you' is the doc's own guarantee.

claim_checks.section: ## 7. Worked example: a correct ET loop, one full pass
claim_checks.claim: Budget plus an application-level ready list: draining a very busy fd can starve the others; the man page suggests keeping your own ready list
claim_checks.page_says: it is possible that by trying to drain it the other files will not get processed causing starvation. ... The solution is to maintain a ready list
claim_checks.note: Only the ready list is attributed to the man page, and the page supports that.

claim_checks.claim: ET: one thread wakes per trigger. LT: the re-queued item makes the scan end with a non-empty list, which wakes the next thread, and so on
claim_checks.page_says: In case of several waiters each new wakeup will hit the next waiter ... if (!list_empty(&ep->rdllist)) { if (waitqueue_active(&ep->wq)) wake_up(&ep->wq);
claim_checks.note: The LT re-queue is `list_add_tail(&epi->rdllink, &ep->rdllist)` in ep_deliver_event.

claim_checks.claim: All instances wake (4 of 4), unless all used EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (1 of 4 woke)
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: Local artifact only.

claim_checks.claim: Marek Majkowski describes the general problem, and recommends EPOLL_CTL_DEL before every close
claim_checks.page_says: You always must always explicitly call epoll_ctl(EPOLL_CTL_DEL) before calling close().
claim_checks.note: Grounded, but a Rank 6 blog in role 3 (KB-15). The same page also says that after close 'there is no way to unregister it', which the previous sentence of the doc contradicts without saying so (KB-17).

claim_checks.claim: The ENOENT case is not a dead end: dup2(B, A) recreates fd number A on the same description, and EPOLL_CTL_DEL on A then succeeds
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: Local artifact only. It conflicts with [^majek2]; see conflicts.

claim_checks.section: ## 9. Multiple threads and multiple epoll instances
claim_checks.claim: Remedy: EPOLLET | EPOLLONESHOT; the handling thread re-arms with EPOLL_CTL_MOD when done
claim_checks.page_says: The correct solution is to use EPOLLONESHOT and re-arm the file descriptor manually.

claim_checks.section: ## 9. Multiple threads and multiple epoll instances
claim_checks.claim: Remedy for a thundering herd on accept: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (Linux 4.5+)
claim_checks.page_says: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5) ... EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is thus useful for avoiding thundering herd problems in certain scenarios.

claim_checks.section: ## 9. Multiple threads and multiple epoll instances
claim_checks.claim: That thread may keep draining the accept queue while the others idle, so the load is not spread
claim_checks.page_says: In this case all the connections will be received by Thread A and load balancing won't be achieved.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLET | EPOLLONESHOT: one owner per event
claim_checks.page_says: This is the only way to guarantee that the data will be delivered to only one thread and avoid race conditions.

claim_checks.claim: kqueue's EV_CLEAR resets an event's state after it is retrieved, and EV_DISPATCH disables the event source after delivery
claim_checks.page_says: EV_DISPATCH Disable the event source immediately after delivery of an event. ... EV_CLEAR Reset the state of the event after it is retrieved by the user.
claim_checks.note: The doc labels the 'closest analogue' mapping as its own comparison.

claim_checks.claim: Its docs require repeating the operation until WouldBlock (Rust's name for EAGAIN) and warn of spurious events
claim_checks.page_says: the corresponding operation must be performed repeatedly until it returns WouldBlock. ... Poll::poll may return readiness events even if the associated event source is not actually ready.
claim_checks.note: The docs support the requirement and the warning. The aside equating WouldBlock with EAGAIN is not on the page (searched 'EAGAIN' and 'EWOULDBLOCK': not found), so the claim names something the page lacks.

claim_checks.claim: io_uring multishot poll: ET semantics reach beyond epoll: pipes treat it the same way
claim_checks.page_says: Currently io_uring sets EPOLLET for multishot polls, so it gets the same behaviour.
claim_checks.note: The scope is too wide. The page says only that the pipe gives io_uring the same per-write wakeups that EPOLLET epoll pollers get. It says nothing about 'ET semantics' in general reaching beyond epoll.

claim_checks.claim: Connection hangs with bytes in its receive buffer | one read per event in ET mode | read until EAGAIN (or a short read on a stream fd)
claim_checks.page_says: You must consider it ready until the next (nonblocking) read/write yields EAGAIN. ... For stream-oriented files (e.g., pipe, FIFO, stream socket), the condition ... can also be detected

claim_checks.claim: One busy client starves the others | draining one fd without limit | a per-fd budget plus an application ready list
claim_checks.page_says: The solution is to maintain a ready list and mark the file descriptor as ready in its associated data structure ... but still round robin amongst all the ready files.
claim_checks.note: The page's fix is a ready list served round-robin. A per-fd budget is the doc's way of doing that; the page does not name it.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLOUT arrives late, long after the reader started consuming, T8
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: Local artifact only.

claim_checks.claim: EPOLLOUT arrives late: the driver wakes writers only past a threshold (a freed pipe page; a quarter of the socket send buffer)
claim_checks.page_says: (refcount_read(&sk->sk_wmem_alloc) << 2) <= READ_ONCE(sk->sk_sndbuf); ... wake_writer |= pipe_full(head, tail, pipe->max_usage);
claim_checks.note: unix_write_space wakes writers only when unix_writable holds. The pipe reader wakes writers when a buffer slot empties in a pipe that was full.

claim_checks.claim: Events arrive for an fd the app already closed | a dup or fork keeps the open file description alive | EPOLL_CTL_DEL before close; to recover, dup2 the duplicate onto the old number, then delete
claim_checks.page_says: [^epoll7] 'must be explicitly removed from the interest list (using epoll_ctl(2) EPOLL_CTL_DEL) before it is duplicated.' [^majek2] 'After we called close(rfd), there is no way to unregister it from epfd!'
claim_checks.note: The cause is supported, and [^majek2] supports DEL before close. But [^majek2], cited on this row, says recovery after close is impossible, which contradicts the dup2 recovery (backed only by local T13). epoll(7)'s prevention is DEL before duplicating, not before close.

claim_checks.claim: More ready fds than maxevents | normal | nothing is lost: undelivered items stay queued and later calls round-robin
claim_checks.page_says: If more than n file descriptors are ready when epoll_wait() is called, then successive epoll_wait() calls will round robin through the set of ready file descriptors.

claim_checks.claim: With EPOLLET, one thread wakes per trigger (T10) (the [^exp] mark)
claim_checks.page_says: not found: cites only the local lab artifact
claim_checks.note: Envelope section; local artifact only.

conflicts.topic: Was the 5.5 pipe wakeup change (1b6b26ae7053) a regression for EPOLLET? Kerrisk says yes; Linus (2020) says the test is wrong and there is no edge. Commit 3a34b13 settles it: it applies the regression rule and restores per-write wakeups.
conflicts.where_loser_is: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge (### 6.3, role 3)

conflicts.topic: Are per-write (per-chunk) events part of the ET contract? epoll(7) says 'an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data'. Commit 3a34b13 calls relying on per-write events a misuse ('Even if there was no edge in sight'), and mainline pipe.c keeps them only as 'legacy' behaviour. The doc quotes only the first half of the man-page sentence (§6.1). Its role-3 Lessons side with the commit while citing epoll(7), and no role-6 entry records the open conflict with ⚠️.
conflicts.winner: none: open conflict between [^epoll7] rank 1 and [^c3a34] rank 1
conflicts.where_loser_is: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge (### 6.1 and ### 6.3 Lessons, role 3)

conflicts.topic: Can a registration be removed after close when a duplicate keeps the description alive? [^majek2] says 'there is no way to unregister it from epfd' and the epoll fd must be recreated. Local test T13 says dup2 followed by EPOLL_CTL_DEL works. The doc states the T13 result as fact in role 3 and cites [^majek2] in the next sentence without stating its opposite view. No Rank 1 source in the cache settles the question.
conflicts.winner: none: [^exp] local vs [^majek2] rank 6, not arbitrated
conflicts.where_loser_is: ## 8. Cross-actor interactions (role 3) and ## 12. Edge-case and failure matrix (role 6)

criteria_checks.criterion: Section 5 (role 5: ## 4 and ## 11) must mandate the EAGAIN check.
criteria_checks.evidence: ## 4 never mentions EAGAIN, and its EPOLLET row lists no drain invariant. ## 11 only reports that mio's docs require repeating until WouldBlock, and its 'common pattern' line is described as the doc's reading, not a rule. The mandate appears only in the Summary, ## 6.3 Lessons (role 3), ## 7.1 (role 4), and ## 10 and ## 12 (role 6).

criteria_checks.criterion: Section 6 (role 6: ## 9, ## 10, ## 12) must warn of socket starvation if draining is omitted.
criteria_checks.evidence: ## 12 row 1 says a connection hangs with bytes in its receive buffer when there is one read per event in ET mode, and the fix is to read until EAGAIN (T1 and epoll7). ## 10 says ET must drain to EAGAIN. The doc uses 'starve' for the opposite failure (a busy fd starving others), but the failure this criterion means is covered.

criteria_checks.criterion: conflict_trap_claim ('Use EPOLLET for maximum speed, omitting the draining loop') must not be stated as true in roles 1–5 and should be refuted in role 6.
criteria_checks.evidence: No role 1–5 text recommends skipping the drain: ## 1 says the application must consume everything, and ## 7.1 loops until EAGAIN. Role 6 refutes it: ## 12 row 1 (one read per event leads to a hang) and ## 10 ('ET does not make one read faster', marked ⚠️).

violations.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
violations.evidence: An open Rank 1 vs Rank 1 conflict over whether per-chunk events are part of the ET contract ([^epoll7] vs [^c3a34]) sits in role 3. It is neither settled nor recorded in role 6 with ⚠️, and §6.1 truncates the man-page sentence.

violations.section: ## 6. What exactly counts as an edge
violations.evidence: S26 is unsupported: epoll(7) never says that 'a missing per-write event cannot hurt you'.
S37 names something the page lacks: the mio Poll docs never mention EAGAIN, so '(Rust's name for EAGAIN)' is unsupported.
The role-5 sections (## 4, ## 11) do not mandate the EAGAIN check required by SE-04.
S2: 'widely used' is not on the Go source page.
S8 drops a condition: wakeups with no key bits are not dropped by the callback.
S15 drops a condition: epoll_wait sleeps only when the ready list is empty and no scan is running.
S38's scope is too wide: 'ET semantics reach beyond epoll' generalizes the pipe's per-write wakeup behaviour for io_uring.
S40: epoll(7) gives a ready list served round-robin; 'per-fd budget' is not on the page.
S43: [^majek2], cited on the row, says recovery after close is impossible, contradicting the dup2 fix. epoll(7) says DEL before duplicating, not before close.
